# qrwty web

- ID: `qrwty-web`
- Template: `web-app@0.1.0`
- Directory: `frontends/qrwty-web/`
- Owned paths: `frontends/qrwty-web/`

## Implementation notes

Build the qrwty user interface in this web app. Use the generated `qrwtyClient` from
`useApis()` and the existing runtime config. Do not generate QR codes in the browser and do not
edit generated clients, contracts, or server code.

Auth
- On load, call GET /auth/session. If 401, show a register/login form; if 200, show the app.
- Register and login with email + password. Store the returned csrfToken in memory (not localStorage).
- Logout calls POST /auth/logout with the csrf token and clears the local state.
- Every mutation sends `x-csrf-token` and uses the same-origin client. Handle 401 by returning to auth.

QR list
- GET /api/qr?limit=25, newest first. Show title (or "Untitled"), destination, created time, and
  the public link `window.location.origin + "/q/" + id`.
- Support the next cursor with a Load more button; empty state; loading and error states.

Create
- Form: destination (required, absolute HTTP/HTTPS, no credentials) and optional title (max 120).
- POST /api/qr; on 201 clear the form, refresh the list, and show the public link.
- Inline 400 errors; 401 returns to auth.

Edit
- Select a QR with its row select button. Only the selected row shows the edit form, the image
  download, and the activity action.
- Edit the selected QR's destination and title, PATCH /api/qr/{id}. Send destination and title; the
  server preserves an omitted optional title and clears it when the request sends null.
- On success refresh the row and keep it selected so its download and activity actions stay
  available; 400/404 inline; 401 returns to auth.

Image
- Shown only for the selected row. Download GET /api/qr/{id}/image through the same-origin client
  with `parseAs: "blob"` (or an authenticated same-origin fetch if the generated client cannot type
  it).
- Trigger a browser download with the returned blob; do not build the image from the destination.
- Show the stable public link beside the download action.

Activity
- Shown only for the selected row. Activity view: from/to date controls defaulting to the last 30
  UTC days, a total, and a table of every returned day including zero-count days.
- GET /api/qr/{id}/activity?from=...&to=...; handle 400 for an invalid or too-wide range.
- Do not claim unique visitors; label the number as requests.

Quality
- Every action works by mouse. No keyboard-only controls.
- No console.error for expected 400/401/404 flows.
- Keep supplemental tests in the app's `tests/` folder: auth gate, list/create, image download,
  activity rendering.
- Do not add a chart library for the first proof; a table is enough.

Test hooks (fixed browser acceptance relies on these exact attributes)
- Email input: `data-testid="auth-email"`; password input: `data-testid="auth-password"`.
- Register button: `data-testid="auth-register"`; login button: `data-testid="auth-login"`.
- Logout button: `data-testid="auth-logout"`.
- Create form: `data-testid="qr-create-form"`, destination `data-testid="qr-destination"`,
  title `data-testid="qr-title"`, submit `data-testid="qr-create"`.
- Each list row: `data-testid="qr-row"` with `data-qr-id` set to the resource id, and a select
  button `data-testid="qr-select"`.
- Edit form on the selected row: destination `data-testid="qr-edit-destination"`, title
  `data-testid="qr-edit-title"`, save `data-testid="qr-edit-save"`.
- Inside the selected row, a download image link or button: `data-testid="qr-image-download"` (a
  link with `download` is fine) and an activity button `data-testid="qr-activity"`.
- Activity form: from `data-testid="activity-from"`; to
  `data-testid="activity-to"`; apply `data-testid="activity-apply"`; total
  `data-testid="activity-total"`; table rows `data-testid="activity-day"` with
  `data-date` and `data-count` attributes.
- The public link shown for a row: `data-testid="qr-public-link"` with its href and text equal to
  `window.location.origin + "/q/" + id`.

Studio (P17)
- Add an owner-only Studio for the selected QR using the generated readQrStudio, previewQrArtwork, saveQrArtwork and exportQrArtwork operations. Use the pinned @jeeves/qr-artwork settings and @jeeves/product-ui configuration editor artifact. Keep drafts in session memory across library navigation; export only saved settings; preserve existing QR-09 hooks and legacy download. Never generate QR artwork in the browser. PNG/SVG bytes arrive from the server in typed base64 envelopes.

# Working with a web-app element

This is a React single-page app (Vite, TypeScript) running on `@jeeves/web-runtime`. In its
container, nginx serves the build and forwards the app's API calls to the services it uses.

## Where things go

- **Pages and components:** `src/pages/` and `src/components/`; the layout and routing are in
  `src/App.tsx`. Add a router (for example `react-router`) when there's more than one page:
  nginx already serves the app for any path.
- **Calling a service:** through its generated client (one per rest-api-client attachment; see
  that template's guide). In components, get clients from `useApis()` so tests can swap them:

  ```tsx
  import { useApis } from "@jeeves/web-runtime";
  import type { app } from "../jeeves.generated.ts";

  export function LinkList() {
    const { links } = useApis<typeof app.apis>();
    // e.g. in an effect: const { data, error } = await links.GET("/links");
  }
  ```

- **Settings that differ per environment** come from the runtime config: `useRuntimeConfig()`
  (or `runtimeConfig()` outside components). The title is `APP_TITLE`; API addresses are in
  `apis`. Don't bake them into the build with `import.meta.env`.
- **Errors:** the whole app is inside an `ErrorBoundary`; wrap risky parts in their own
  `<ErrorBoundary fallback={(error, reset) => ...}>` so one failure doesn't blank the page.
- **Styles:** `src/styles.css` is plain CSS. Adding a UI library is fine; pin its version.
- **Tests:** `test/*.test.tsx` with Vitest; render components inside
  `<JeevesProvider config={...} apis={{ links: fakeClient }}>`.
- **Dependencies:** add npm packages to this app's `package.json` with exact versions.
- **Running it locally:** `npm run dev`. Set `API_<TARGET>_URL` to each service's published
  address (`docker compose port <service> <port>`) so the dev server can forward API calls.

## Don't

- Don't edit `src/jeeves.generated.ts`, `src/clients/*.generated.ts`, anything in `nginx/`,
  `docker-compose.yml`, or `vendor/`. They're generated from the design and overwritten.
- Don't call services by their own URLs or with plain `fetch`; go through the generated client
  (the browser can only reach them through `/_api/<service>/`).
- Don't remove the `startApp(...)` call in `src/main.tsx` or the `#root` element.
- Don't put secrets in the app: everything in it is visible to users. Tokens for APIs are added
  by nginx.
- Don't log with `console.error` for expected situations: Jeeves's checks fail on console errors.

## Checks Jeeves runs

The page loads with no console errors, any path serves the app, the runtime config comes from
the container's environment and is applied (the page title), and for each connected service a
sample call through its client renders a result on `/_jeeves/status`.

# Working with a rest-api-client attachment

This element calls another service's REST API through a typed client. The client is generated
from the design (`src/clients/<target>.generated.ts`, exported as `<target>Client`), and its
types come from the target's contract (`contracts/<target>.openapi.yaml`).

## Calling the API

```ts
import { linksClient } from "../../clients/links.generated.ts";

const { data, error, response } = await linksClient.GET("/links/{code}", {
  params: { path: { code } },
});
if (error) {
  // A documented error status: `error` is typed from the contract (e.g. NOT_FOUND).
}
```

- Paths, parameters, bodies, and responses are typed from the contract, relative to the
  target API's base path. An error status comes back as `{ error, response }`; it isn't thrown.
- A call that gets no response throws a `RestClientError` (import it from `@jeeves/rest-client`)
  with `code` `TIMEOUT` (no answer within the attachment's `timeoutMs`) or `NETWORK`. Handle it
  where a failed dependency should degrade gracefully instead of failing the whole request.
- Idempotent calls (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE) are retried `retries` times after a
  timeout, a network error, or a 502/503/504. POST and PATCH never are.
- **In a service**, calls made while handling a request forward its `x-request-id`, so one ID
  follows a request across services in the logs. The address and token come from
  `API_<TARGET>_URL` and `API_<TARGET>_TOKEN`, set by docker-compose.yml and checked at startup.
- **In a web app**, the client calls the API through the app's own server
  (`/_api/<target>/...`, proxied by nginx, which also adds the bearer token). Get clients from
  `useApis()` in components so tests can pass fakes through `<JeevesProvider apis={...}>`.

## When the contract changes

`npm run typecheck` (or `pnpm typecheck`) first regenerates `src/clients/<target>.openapi.ts`
from the contract (its `pretypecheck` script runs `jeeves-rest-client-types`), then type-checks.
After the target's contract changes, run it: calls that no longer match show up as type errors.

- **Legacy contract (project-owned):** if the operation you need isn't in the contract, add it to
  the contract (and implement it in the target service) rather than calling an undocumented path.
- **Generated resource contract:** the contract is generated-owned. Do **not** add operations or
  edit it. Use the declared operations; if something is missing, stop and say so.

## Binary responses

An image operation returns `image/png`. Ask the client for a blob (or use an authenticated
same-origin `fetch` if the generated types cannot express it):

```ts
const { data } = await qrwtyClient.GET("/api/qr/{id}/image", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  parseAs: "blob",
});
```

Do not decode or generate the image in the browser.


## Don't

- Don't edit `src/clients/*.generated.ts` or `src/clients/*.openapi.ts`; both are regenerated.
- Don't build URLs to other services by hand or call them with plain `fetch`; use the client.
- Don't read `API_*` variables yourself or hard-code service addresses.

## Checks Jeeves runs

The generated client type-checks against the target's contract, a documented GET (`/ping` when
there is one) succeeds through the client inside compose, and a call that gets no answer fails
with a typed timeout error.
